prompt:
$f(x)=\begin{cases}x^{2}, & x\le1\\ ax+b, & x>1\end{cases}$

Find $a$ and $b$ so that $f$ is both continuous and differentiable at $x=1$.
markscheme:
Continuity: $1=a+b$ **(M1)**

Differentiability: the one-sided gradients agree: $2(1)=a$ **(M1)**, so $a=2$ **(A1)**, $b=-1$ **(A1)**

Continuity alone is not enough: $|x|$ is continuous at 0 but has a corner there, so it is not differentiable.

prompt:
**(a)** Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{3x^{2}+1}{2x^{2}-x}$. **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac1x$ does not exist. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Divide by $x^{2}$: $\dfrac{3+1/x^{2}}{2-1/x}\to\dfrac32$ **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** As $x\to0^{+}$, $\frac1x\to+\infty$; as $x\to0^{-}$, $\frac1x\to-\infty$; the function does not approach a finite value **(R1)**
